_comment: FA -- flattened audio. Every person in the group gets their own audio part and
their own gallery image, each introduced by text naming whose it is. The person
of interest is named UP FRONT, before anyone else is shown.
The turn this produces, for a group of participants 1, 3 and 4 with 3 as the
person of interest:
text   video_intro                 video  <sampled frames>
text   poa_audio_intro             audio  <participant 3's track>
text   poa_image_intro             image  <participant_3.png>
text   others_intro
text   other_open(1)   audio <1>   text other_between   image <1>   text other_close
text   other_open(4)   audio <4>   text other_between   image <4>   text other_close
text   user_prompt_template
The system prompt is folded into video_intro, not into the closing block: this
prompt opens by saying what the model is about to be shown, so that is where a
standing instruction belongs.
EVERY FRAGMENT BELOW IS A REAL TEXT PART sitting immediately before the media it
introduces. That is what binds an id to a track, and it is why FA does not
repeat PA's inert '<audio1>' markers. Rewording a fragment is fine; dropping the
id out of one is not.
Placeholders available in every fragment:
{participant}  the person of interest, in every fragment including the ones
describing somebody else
{speaker_id}   the person THIS fragment introduces
An unknown placeholder is left as itself rather than raising.
user_prompt_template additionally gets, from modes/fa.py:
{goa_ids}      every id in the group, comma-separated, ascending
{other_ids}    the group minus the person of interest
{goa_size}     how many people are in the group
({conversation_floor} does NOT render: the flattener keeps only scalars, and it
is a list.)
poa_intro_video_only replaces poa_audio_intro + poa_image_intro under --no-audio,
where there is no track to introduce. Keep it naming the participant.
system_prompt: You are a helpful multimodal assistant.
video_intro:
Watch the 30-second video clip and listen to the provided audio. Identify the intentions of the indicated participant.

An intention is what the participant appears to want to achieve, based on what they seem to believe is happening and what they seem to want. Focus on intentions, not just visible actions.

The following is a video that shows the conversation from top view:
poa_audio_intro: This is the participant that you would observe: participant {participant}, and this is their audio in the conversation:
poa_image_intro: This is an image of them:
poa_intro_video_only: This is the participant that you would observe: participant {participant}. This is an image of them:
others_intro: These are all other participants that are within the same conversation as participant {participant}:
user_prompt_template:
You can use the gallery images to locate the participants in the video.

Use observable visual and audio cues, the overall tone of the interaction, the situation type, and likely social scripts to support your interpretation. Give your best intuition even when the intention is subtle or ambiguous.

Identify the intentions of participant {participant}.

For each intention you identify, answer in this format:

1. Timestamps: [start time] [end time]
2. Intention: [brief description of what the participant is trying to do or achieve]
3. Confidence in interpretation: [1-5]
4. Why: [observable cues plus your interpretation of the participant's beliefs/desires and the situation]
5. Confidence in explanation: [1-5]
6. Intensity: [1-5 rating of how strong or high-priority the intention appears]
7. Counterfactual explanation: [an alternative interpretation that would change the understood intention]

If the full clip contains no clear intention, answer only:

No clear intention: yes
Why: [brief explanation]
